title: REPAIR: precedent.py silently discards extra --voids targets (non-accumulating flag)
description: Discovered by the coordinator publishing PR-032: precedent.py publish accepts multiple --voids flags but keeps only the LAST, exiting 0 and recording one relation where two were requested - a silent discard of an explicit instruction, the same defect family as a false-green test. --dicta, --sources, --tier-evidence and --cites accumulate on the same subcommand, so the semantics are inconsistent and the trap is invisible. Fix: either make --voids (and any other single-value relation flag with the same shape: --overrules, --supersedes, --reinterprets, --revalues, --distinguishes, --follows, --cites where applicable) accumulate with paired --controlling-authority positional matching, OR refuse the publish with a clear message when more targets are supplied than the tool will honor. Refusing is acceptable and simpler; silent discard is not. Audit every relation flag on publish for the same shape and state the audit result in the handoff. Acceptance: python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p 'test_precedent*.py' -v green with nonzero count plus a new test proving a two-target publish either records both relations or refuses; py_compile clean; PR-032 and PR-033's existing relations untouched (immutable class A).

notes.note:
HANDOFF -> verifier: T-376 DONE by coordinator-opus. Handing to a DISTINCT verifier: I am the producer and must not verdict.

WHAT WAS WRONG. publish accepted --voids A --voids B, kept only B, exited 0, wrote ONE
relation where two were requested. Silent discard of an explicit instruction into an
immutable record.

THE AUDIT THE TASK ASKED FOR, and it changes the scope. I introspected every flag on the
publish subcommand mechanically rather than by eye. 47 flags total: 12 accumulate
(action=append), 2 are booleans, and 33 have the silent-discard shape. Not five relation
flags. The full list is reproducible with the script quoted below. Because 12 flags on the
same subcommand DO accumulate, the semantics were inconsistent and the trap was invisible
from outside: nothing in the help text distinguishes a flag that accumulates from one that
overwrites.

WHAT I SHIPPED. A StoreOnce argparse action that refuses a repeat with a message naming the
flag, the defect id, and the workaround. Applied via _refuse_repeats(p_pub, p_conf) to every
single-value flag on the two verbs that WRITE a record. Read-only verbs and --root are left
alone so a wrapper that repeats --root still behaves.

TWO DELIBERATE DECISIONS A VERIFIER SHOULD ATTACK.

1. REFUSE rather than ACCUMULATE. The task allowed either. I chose refuse because
   accumulation is not a one-line change: --voids pairs with --controlling-authority, and
   --overrules and --revalues pair with --factor and --factor-note, so accumulating needs
   occurrence-order pairing. This module's own docstring already carries a DEVIATION note
   about how fragile that pairing is for --distinguishes. A second fragile pairing surface
   is a worse trade than an explicit refusal. THE COST IS REAL AND I AM NOT HIDING IT: a
   record that legitimately voids two targets can no longer be expressed as one act. The
   schema would allow it, since relations is a list. If the verifier thinks that cost is
   too high, this is the right place to say so.

2. UNIFORM rather than scoped to the relation flags. Fixing five siblings and leaving 28
   with the identical trap on the same subcommand is the half-repair shape this registry
   keeps finding. This widens the task as written, so it is called out rather than slipped
   in. The empirical check for blast radius: the whole precedent suite passes unchanged.

EVIDENCE, replayable.
  python3 -m py_compile .harness/bin/precedent.py                      -> exit 0
  python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_precedent*.py"
      -> Ran 252 tests, OK. Nonzero count, green, nothing depended on the discard.
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/ -q                                 -> 527 passed, 4 skipped
  Two --voids now: "precedent.py publish: error: --voids was given more than once and this
      flag takes a single value ... If you need two targets, publish two acts." exit nonzero.
  One --voids: parsing succeeds and the run proceeds to the next legitimate validation
      ("refused: tier_evidence must be non-empty"), which is the proof the guard did not
      break the single use.

NEW TEST: .harness/tests/test_precedent_repeat_flags.py, 13 tests, grouped by what each
protects: the reported defect on --voids, the 15 siblings sampled from the audit, the flags
that must STILL accumulate (the regression this fix could plausibly cause), and that nothing
is written when a repeat is refused.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, because a guard nobody broke on purpose is not a verified guard:
  removing _refuse_repeats entirely      -> 5 of 13 fail
  dropping p_conf from the guard         -> 1 of 13 fails
Both directions caught. Restored after.

IMMUTABILITY. PR-032 and PR-033 were not touched; a test asserts both still parse and carry
their relations. No file under .harness/precedents/ was written by this task.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. I did not add accumulation for any relation flag, and I did not touch the
33-flag audit result into a task of its own, because the uniform fix already covers all 33.
If the verifier prefers accumulation for --voids specifically, that is a new task, not a
correction of this one.
